newsitem.title: USA: Marvel bond holders win court decision.
newsitem.headline: Marvel bond holders win court decision.

text.p: A judge on Friday rejected a request by Marvel Entertainment Group Inc's banks and management for an emergency order to block bond holders led by Carl Icahn from taking control of the board of directors.
In a ruling from the bench after a hearing, Judge Helen Balick of U.S. Bankruptcy Court denied the request for a restraining order.
She said she did not believe the banks would succeed on the merits of their claim that Marvel would be irreparably harmed by having the bond holders take control.

Bond holder attorney James Spiotto told Reuters, "The court recognized that there was no basis to prevent the bond holders from voting the shares for a new board that would maximize the value of Marvel Entertainment."
The bond holders already had possession of the 80 percent of Marvel Entertainment shares that secured their nearly $900 million in face value of bonds of Marvel Holdings Inc.

Marvel spokesman Michael Freitag said, "We intend to appeal this decision and are seeking a temporary restraining order from the U.S. District Court to maintain the status quo until our appeal can be heard."
During the hearing, the attorney for the lead Marvel bank, Chase Manhattan, told Balick that control by the Icahn group would amount to a hostile takeover.

Attorney Douglas Leibhafsky said, "These properties belong to the banks. We're prepared to prove that and we're not going to be blackmailed." He promised further litigation for control of the Marvel Entertainment assets.
The Marvel Entertainment banks are secured lenders with a $610 million claim against the company.
In her ruling, Balick said she would stop automatic monthly payment to all lawyers and other professionals because of the see-saw legal battles being waged over Marvel.
"I am disturbed by the frequency of past litigation in several courts...(and consider it) an abuse of the bankruptcy system," Balick said.
